items.title: Quantum algorithms for multidimensional partial differential equations
items.subtitle: Quantum linear-algebra methods for scientific PDE workloads
items.summary: Research on quantum methods for solving multidimensional PDEs, including circuit-efficient formulations, practical case studies, and singular-value-based approaches.
overview: This research explores how quantum linear-algebra techniques can be used to formulate and solve multidimensional partial differential equations that arise across scientific and engineering applications.
The work emphasizes practical circuit structure, scalability, and validation across representative PDE families rather than treating the quantum algorithm as an isolated mathematical primitive.

sections.heading: Research direction
paragraphs: The central question is how to map structured PDE problems into quantum computations while keeping the circuit construction efficient enough to study on simulators and available hardware.
Recent work extends this direction toward singular-value decomposition and transformation methods for PDEs in areas such as computational fluid dynamics and nuclear physics.

items.title: Cooperative particle track building
items.subtitle: Heuristic and quantum acceleration for high-energy physics reconstruction
items.summary: TrackML reconstruction built around a helical EKF core, cooperative candidate search, and a collection of heuristic optimization methods.
overview: This project studies particle track reconstruction as a search and estimation problem rather than a single fixed pipeline.
Parallel track hypotheses can share quality information and prune weaker candidates while heuristic methods explore alternatives to conventional combinatorial search.

sections.heading: Methods
items: Ant colony and particle swarm optimization

sections.heading: Research objective
paragraphs: The objective is to compare reconstruction quality, execution cost, and search behavior across classical and hybrid approaches for high-pileup tracking workloads.

items.title: mkFit performance and reproducibility benchmarking
items.subtitle: A reproducible harness for track-reconstruction experiments
items.summary: A Docker-first workflow for building, running, comparing, and reporting mkFit variants across controlled scaling and performance experiments.
overview: mkbench is designed to make performance experiments repeatable rather than dependent on a one-off local environment.
The harness packages build and run configuration, geometry artifacts, scaling sweeps, plots, and machine-readable reports so comparisons can be reproduced and audited.

items.title: Statistical validation of rolling risk models
items.subtitle: Backtesting Value-at-Risk forecasts with formal coverage tests
items.summary: A command-line backtesting system for historical and Gaussian Value-at-Risk models using Kupiec and Christoffersen statistical tests.
overview: This work treats risk forecasts as statistical claims that should be tested rather than accepted from a model output alone.
The toolkit evaluates rolling Value-at-Risk estimates with unconditional and conditional coverage tests and produces repeatable reporting for model comparison.
